  "content_type": "ethical_teaching",
  "chunks": [
    {
      "chunk_type": "isnad",
      "arabic_text": "وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ زَكَرِيَّا الْمُؤْمِنِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ",
      "translations": {
        "en": "And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Ibrahim ibn Sahil, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:"
      }
    },
    {
      "chunk_type": "body",
      "arabic_text": "«الْحَاجُّ وَالْمُعْتَمِرُ وَفْدُ اللَّهِ إِنْ سَأَلُوهُ أَعْطَاهُمْ وَإِنْ دَعَوْهُ أَجَابَهُمْ وَإِنْ شَفَعُوا شَفَّعَهُمْ وَإِنْ سَكَتُوا ابْتَدَأَهُمْ وَيُعَوَّضُونَ بِالِدْرْهَمِ أَلْفَ أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ».",
      "translations": {
        "en": "The pilgrim (Hajj) and the visitor (Umrah) are the guests/deputies of God; if they ask Him, He gives them; if they call upon Him, He answers them; if they intercede, He accepts their intercession; if they remain silent, He initiates (bestowing upon them); and they are compensated for a single Dirham with a million Dirhams."
      }
    }
  ],
  "translations": {
    "en": {
      "summary": "This hadith highlights the spiritual status of the pilgrim (Hajj) and the visitor (Umrah) as 'guests of God' (Wafd Allah). It enumerates four specific divine favors bestowed upon them: answering their requests, responding to their calls, accepting their intercession, and initiating blessings even if they remain silent. Additionally, it mentions a spiritual compensation where a single Dirham is rewarded with a million Dirhams.",
      "seo_question": "What are the specific spiritual rewards and statuses granted to the Hajj and Umrah pilgrims in Shia tradition?",
      "key_terms": {
        "الْحَاجُّ": "The pilgrim (one performing Hajj)",
        "وَالْمُعْتَمِرُ": "And the visitor (one performing Umrah)",
        "وَفْدُ اللَّهِ": "Guests or deputies of God",
        "وَفْد": "Guests/Deputies",
        "إِنْ سَأَلُوهُ أَعْطَاهُمْ": "If they ask, He gives",
